title: Why Does a Chick-fil-A Cost Only $10,000 to Open?
description:
Chick-fil-A operators put up just $10,000, but the company keeps the land, the building and the equipment, then takes 15% of sales and half of the profit that's left.
#chickfila #franchise #business #shorts

Sources: Chick-fil-A 2026 Franchise Disclosure Document via Franchise Chatter (Sep 2026); The Atlanta Journal-Constitution (Apr 9, 2026); Restaurant Business (2026); Food Republic (Apr 24, 2026); The Hustle (Jun 24, 2024); Business Insider via AOL (Apr 2017); InvestmentGrade (Sep 2026)
Photos: ccPixs.com, JeepersMedia (Mike Mozart), Kzoo Cowboy (CC BY 2.0, Flickr); Generic Brand Productions, j.reed (CC BY-SA 2.0, Flickr)

first_comment: Be honest: would you run a Chick-fil-A for $10K and half the profit, or pass? 🐔

scenes.say: A Chick-fil-A selling {$9 million|nine million} a year costs {$10,000|ten grand}.
scenes.source: $10,000: Chick-fil-A 2026 FDD Item 5 via Franchise Chatter Sep 2026 ('Initial Franchise Fee: $10,000'); Business Insider via AOL ('charges franchisees only $10,000 to open a new restaurant'); Food Republic Apr 24 2026. $9M: AJC Apr 9 2026 (freestanding restaurants 'almost $9.2 million in 2025'); Franchise Chatter (2026 FDD Item 19: non-mall average $9,161,239 across 2,302 units); Restaurant Business ('just under $9.2 million')

scenes.say: That's the average standalone store, and it's closed every single Sunday.
scenes.source: AJC Apr 9 2026 ('restaurants that are closed on Sunday'); InvestmentGrade Sep 2026 ('Restaurants close on Sundays'); averages as in scene 1

scenes.say: So why would Chick-fil-A hand one over to you for {$10,000|ten grand}?

scenes.source: Food Republic Apr 24 2026 ('all of it belongs to the company ... the owner-operators don't earn a financial interest in their franchise'); The Hustle Jun 24 2024 ('Chick-fil-A pays for (and retains ownership of) everything')

scenes.say: Chick-fil-A pays for the land, the building, the kitchen equipment, and it keeps all of it.
scenes.source: Business Insider via AOL ('pays for all startup costs — including real estate, restaurant construction, and equipment'); The Hustle Jun 24 2024 ('pays for (and retains ownership of) everything — real estate, equipment, inventory'); InvestmentGrade Sep 2026 (building, equipment and furnishings stay Chick-fil-A's; land is Chick-fil-A's or a third party's, never the operator's)

scenes.say: Then it takes {15%|fifteen percent} of every sale,
scenes.source: Chick-fil-A 2026 FDD Item 6 via Franchise Chatter (Base Operating Service Fee: 15% of Gross Receipts, net of equipment rental); Business Insider via AOL ('15% of sales plus 50% of pretax profit remaining'); Food Republic Apr 24 2026 ('15% of annual sales and 50% of the profit'); The Hustle Jun 24 2024

scenes.say: plus half of the profit that's left.
scenes.source: Chick-fil-A 2026 FDD Item 6 via Franchise Chatter (Additional Operating Service Fee: '50% of the Net Profit'); Business Insider via AOL ('50% of pretax profit remaining'); Food Republic Apr 24 2026; The Hustle Jun 24 2024

scenes.say: And most operators are only allowed to run one store.
scenes.source: Business Insider via AOL ('prohibits most of its franchisees from opening multiple units'); The Hustle Jun 24 2024 ('In most cases, they aren't permitted to own multiple locations'); Food Republic Apr 24 2026 ('usually aren't allowed to operate more than one restaurant')

scenes.say: So ten grand doesn't buy you a restaurant. It buys you a job running theirs.
scenes.source: Point of view drawn from the ownership and fee facts above; no new figure
